title: Memorandum on Rural Home Loans Note Forms and the Measure of the Late Charge
content:
**Memorandum.** How the gross late charge on a Rural Home Loans loan is measured depends on the note the loan was closed on, and the note follows from the loan's opening date on the loan record.

## Note forms in the portfolio

1. **Former rural residence note.** A loan opened before 2016-01-01 was closed on the association's former rural residence note, which sets a flat late charge of 25.00 USD as the gross charge whatever the late charge rate.
2. **Association installment note.** A loan opened on or after 2016-01-01 and before 2021-01-01 was closed on the association's own installment note, which measures the charge on the whole monthly installment, the monthly principal-and-interest payment and the monthly escrow deposit on the loan record together, multiplied by the late charge rate and divided by 100.
3. **Uniform secondary-market note.** Any other loan, opened on or after 2021-01-01, was closed on the uniform secondary-market note, which measures the charge on the monthly principal-and-interest payment on the loan record alone, multiplied by the late charge rate and divided by 100.

The escrow deposit enters the measure of a late charge only where the loan's note measures the charge on the whole monthly installment.

## Opening-date boundaries

| Opening date | Note | Gross charge |
|---|---|---|
| 2015-12-31 | former rural residence note | 25.00 flat |
| 2016-01-01 | association installment note | principal-and-interest plus escrow deposit, times the rate, divided by 100 |
| 2020-12-31 | association installment note | principal-and-interest plus escrow deposit, times the rate, divided by 100 |
| 2021-01-01 | uniform secondary-market note | principal-and-interest alone, times the rate, divided by 100 |

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

A monthly principal-and-interest payment of 1200.00 USD, a monthly escrow deposit of 400.00 USD and a late charge rate of 4 percent:

- on the installment note, 1200.00 plus 400.00 is 1600.00, multiplied by 4 and divided by 100: a gross charge of 64.00;
- on the uniform note, 1200.00 multiplied by 4 and divided by 100: a gross charge of 48.00;
- on the former rural residence note, a gross charge of 25.00, the rate playing no part.
